title.narrative: Second Small Towns Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project

description.narrative: The Project has three components. Component 1 will develop an efficient, effective, and accountable urban water supply and sanitation sector by establishing and implementing policies, establishing service standards, and enhancing sector coordination. Component 2 will entail development of safe, accessible, and adequate water supply and sanitation facilities in about 20 small towns. Component 3 will strengthen governance and capacity for project management and operation.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved, affordable, and sustainable water supply and sanitation services which are governed and managed by locally accountable representative bodies.

1. 240,00 people in 20 small towns have access to high [(i) increased per capita water supply 90-100 liters per capita per day for private house connection; (ii) 24-hour water supply with adequate residual pressure; (iii) at least 90% coverage of the service area after 5 years of operation; (iv) treated water satisfying the National Drinking Water Quality standards (2007); and (v) predominantly private house connections] level water services by 2015. Progress/Status: 370,099 people in 21 towns have access to 100 LPCD and increased supply hours. 20 town projects are supplying treated drinking water
52,398 private connections provided. Data Source: Data from each town complied in ADB project completion report. Household surveys complied in BME reports. Project completion report Government/SEIU reports Baseline value: 0

2. Reduced time for fetching water (essentially to zero in all towns) by 2015. Progress/Status: Through private connections water is available at houses all the time. Data Source: Household surveys Project completion report Baseline value:

3. 270,000 people have access to and use improved sanitation [defined in accordance with JMP, as the system that hygiencially separates human excreta from human contact. Flush or pour-flush toilet to piped sewer system, septic tank or pit latrine with slab, and composting toilet are included] facilities by 2015. Progress/Status: 278,415 people have access to improved sanitation facilities.
Through OBA implementation, 5,056 HH and 49 (Institutional and public) toilets constructed.
ODF declarations in 13 towns have contributed in achieving this outcome. Data Source: Household surveys complied in BME reports Project completion report Government/SEIU reports Baseline value:

4. Wastewater in at least three towns is disposed of in a way that meets environmental standards [tolerance limits of wastewater to be discharged into inland surface waters from combined wastewater treatment plants, set by the Government, will be used. Limits include 50 milligrams per liter (mg/l) for total suspended solids, 50 mgl for biochemical oxygen demand and 5.5-9.0 for pH] by 2015. Progress/Status: DEWAT systems for the wastewater and fecal sludge to meet environmental standards are studied for two towns. Contract for waste water and fecal sludge management have been recently completed in Vyas while it is already completed in Indrapur (Morang). Data Source: Progress reports Review missions Project completion report Baseline value: 0

5. Operation of water supply and wastewater services with full O&M cost recovery is implemented by WUSC in 20 towns. Progress/Status: TDF is supporting all 21 towns in setting water tariff for the full O&M cost recovery. Tariff guidelines prepared
For effective O&M, capacity development trainings have been provided to 21 WUSCs. Data Source: Progress reports Review missions Project completion report Baseline value: N
